gen-silkscreen-gf-sawarabi-gothic: Silkscreen spells everything out in chunky, spaced-apart pixel letters, a lo-fi retro look with one unchanging line weight. Sawarabi Gothic loosens things up with open curves.
gen-silkscreen-gf-shanti: Spaghetti-thin, widely spaced pixel letters give Silkscreen its lo-fi, retro punch up top. Shanti follows with a generous opening in the e and a modern, smooth finish.
gen-silkscreen-gf-shippori-antique-b1: Silkscreen is all blocky retro pixels, crisp and playful with room around each letter, while Shippori Antique B1 keeps daylight showing through every curve. One shouts in a lo-fi voice; the other speaks quietly.
gen-silkscreen-gf-sn-pro: Strokes with no thick-to-thin shift mark Silkscreen out, a lo-fi retro heading that never swells or narrows anywhere. SN Pro supplies open, modern curves underneath.
gen-silkscreen-gf-sour-gummy: Sour Gummy keeps its wide gaps crisp even when tiny. Silkscreen's thin, looping tubing strokes feel retro and lo-fi beside that modern sans-serif, like an old arcade cabinet next to a new phone.
gen-silkscreen-gf-source-sans-3: Pixel-art retro, lo-fi and unmistakable. Source Sans 3 lets its lower a-bowl open up to breathe, so the blocky Silkscreen heading above it feels grounded instead of loud.
gen-silkscreen-gf-spinnaker: Retro pixels, spaced out and lo-fi. Silkscreen has no hairlines at all, while Spinnaker keeps its counters connected to the outside, so bump up the body size a touch if it feels tight.
gen-silkscreen-gf-suse: Silkscreen draws its lo-fi retro letters like spaghetti, thin and spread apart, with nothing thick or thin about them. SUSE rolls on below in rope-thick curves and open bowls, easy going for lengthy text.
gen-silkscreen-gf-suse-mono: SUSE Mono holds clear gaps on both sides of every letter, approachable and professional in tone. And Silkscreen adds its bent-wire strokes up top, a lo-fi retro flourish with constant line weight.
gen-silkscreen-gf-tasa-orbiter: Thickness that never shifts around the curves defines Silkscreen, a lo-fi retro heading built from spaced pixel strokes. And TASA Orbiter matches it with clean, unclogged counters, a crisp pairing of old arcade and modern.
